headline: Andrew Made Sixteen Adds In One Week. Two Were Broncos. The Broncos Were On Bye.
kicker: (110.56, a perfect lineup, 1-12 in all-play. Lost by 63.84, the biggest blowout of the week.)
lede: Andrew added sixteen players in Week 10. At 9:18 on Sunday morning he cut CJ Daniels, added the day before, for J.K. Dobbins. At 1:00 he cut Reggie Virgil, a $1 waiver claim, for Pat Bryant. Dobbins and Bryant both play for Denver. Denver was on bye. Six of his starters were added this week and the lineup was perfect: 110.56, 1-12 in all-play, and a 63.84-point loss to Will, who scored 174.40 and left a 194.64 lineup on the table, 15.36 more than the season high. Chris beat Barrett by 16.96, so the top two are both 18-2. Barrett cleared the median by 0.95 and Nathan missed it by 0.95, a week after it split 0.88 both ways. Chris opened the $95 monument and spent $6. Anuj started Emmett Johnson, finally, for 33.1, and lost by 3.42.
tldr: Andrew made 16 adds. Two were Broncos. Denver was on bye. He lost by 63.84.
Will scored 174.40 and still left a 194.64 lineup on his bench, 15.36 above the season high.
Anuj finally started Emmett Johnson: 33.1. Lost by 3.42.
The median split 0.95 both ways. Last week it was 0.88.

sections.awards: One per team. Nobody got off.
sections.power: Season to date. Best lineup is your record if you had started your best possible lineup every week. The tax is the wins you left on your own bench.
sections.median: Week 10's line was 124.57. Barrett cleared it by 0.95 and Nathan missed it by 0.95. Last week it split 0.88 both ways. Barrett lost his game and got a win here; Greg (Miley) won his and lost here. Six teams swept, six got swept. Right of the line is a win.
sections.standings: Week 10 scoring, both results, and how much of your own roster you managed to start. Efficiency is what you scored over what your best legal lineup would have scored. Injured reserve does not count against you. Four teams hit 100.0 percent: Barrett, Greg (Miley), Andrew and Jon. Andrew and Jon were the two lowest scores in the league.
sections.bench: 126.14 points of lineup regret this week, down from 147.58. Greg (IR) leads with 22.40, mostly Omarion Hampton. Will's 20.24 includes a three-touchdown quarterback.
sections.faab: Every dollar of Week 10, audited. $78 spent, 47 adds, sixteen of them Andrew's. The biggest bid, $30, started and scored 6.14.
sections.money: Auction dollars against everything each player has scored so far, started or not. Brock Purdy: $3, 207.96 points. A.J. Brown: $45, 18.3.
sections.studs: The best and worst starts of Week 10, measured against what Yahoo thought they would do. Christian McCaffrey beat his projection by 27.38. Drake Maye missed his by 18.77.
sections.games: The long version, closest game first.

newsletter.intro: Andrew made sixteen adds and two of them were on a bye. Chris beat Barrett and now they are both 18-2. Will scored 174.40 and still left twenty points on his bench. Find your team below; everyone got one.
next: 18-2 against the hottest team in the league. Darrius has won three straight and was ranked last in August. Barrett has not lost to the median all season.

Nathan has $0 of FAAB and finally benched Cousins correctly. Abhishek has a Sunday morning habit. Both went 0-2 last week.
Sixteen adds against $40 on Corey Kiner. Andrew, check the bye weeks first. Anuj, keep starting Emmett Johnson.
The house reopened against three straight perfect lineups that keep losing. Jon has $8. Tom has Mahomes.
Nishil benched a quarterback he picked up on Monday. Greg (Miley) has $90 and no adds. Somebody spend something.
Four straight losses against the team that just ended six. Maclane, Justice Hill is on your bench again. You know what to do. You have known since Week 3.

games.note: The closest game of the week, 3.42. Anuj finally did it. The Emmett Johnson file, entry five: started, 101 rushing yards, 70 receiving, two touchdowns, 33.1. Four wrong weeks and then the right one, and it lost. Dak Prescott threw five touchdowns for 35.42. Then the rest. Corey Kiner, $30, the biggest bid of the week, started for 6.14. Audric Estime, $10, 3.6 on the bench. $40 of FAAB for 9.74 points. Three tight ends started: Sam LaPorta 2.1, Hunter Henry 3.2 and Mike Gesicki 1.4 at flex. Gesicki cost $21 last week and has 3.5 points in two starts. Nate Landman, a Saturday pickup, 1.0 at IDP. 113.40, 0-2, 2-11 in all-play, and the three-game streak is over. Greg (Miley) started Jared Goff over Bryce Young, the right quarterback for the first time in three weeks: 22.42 to 8.1. Cam Skattebo scored 25.7 and Travis Hunter 10.9 at IDP, with Nick Bolton (9.0) correctly on the bench. A perfect lineup, 100.0 percent. It scored 116.82, missed the median by 7.75, and went 1-1. Sunk by the median, the only team that was.

First place against first place, and Chris took it back. Jahmyr Gibbs ($73) ran for 153 yards and caught 99 more: 42.7, the second-best start of the week. Josh Allen scored 23.34 with Tyler Shough (10.98) on the bench, the right call this time. Tony Pollard 19.9 and Xavier Hutchinson 13.8 at flex. Kyren Williams ($32) ran for 23 yards, 4.2. Malik Nabers 5.9. And the monument has been touched. $95 of FAAB, a monument by last week, and on Wednesday Chris spent $6 of it: Darren Waller ($5) started at tight end for 3.4 and the Ravens ($1) for 7.04. 10.44 points for $6. 142.48, 96.2 percent, 2-0. Barrett played a perfect lineup, 100.0 percent, and it scored 125.52. Chuba Hubbard 31.7, Amon-Ra St. Brown 23.8, Brock Bowers ($39) 2.8, the worst money of the week at tight end. Tre' Harris, added Saturday night, started for 11.1. Six straight head-to-head wins, over. He cleared the median by 0.95, the closest margin in the league, and stays 10-0 against it. Both teams are 18-2.

George Pickens caught eleven balls for 145 yards and three touchdowns: 39.0, the best flex of the week. Chase Brown scored 24.3, DJ Moore 17.4 and Cam Little kicked 170 yards of field goals for 21.0. Then Drake Maye, last week three touchdowns and three interceptions, threw for 48 yards: 3.02 on a 21.79 projection, the worst start of the week. On Monday at 3:38 Nishil added Justin Herbert and benched him. 16.26. Omar Cooper Jr. started and did not record a stat. 22.14 points of regret and 2-0 anyway, 142.96, his second sweep of the season. Maclane lost his fourth straight head-to-head. Aaron Rodgers 15.62, Ryan Flournoy 16.1, Jonathan Taylor ($62) 11.3. Tyler Allgeier started at running back for 1.4. On the bench, a museum: Justice Hill, claimed for $0 on Saturday, the third time Maclane has added him this season, 6.3 a week after he scored 19.5 on Andrew's bench. KaVontae Turpin, claimed for $0 on Friday after Abhishek cut him, 2.72. Demarcus Robinson 0.00. 118.76, 0-2. The best lineup scores 123.66 and also goes 0-2.

Six straight head-to-head losses, and then Greg (IR) drew Jon. Brock Purdy ($3) threw for 389 yards: 31.66. Blake Corum scored 20.4 and Bhayshul Tuten 18.8. The Bills, a $4 Wednesday claim, 14.52. Arvell Reese, $2, 8.5 at IDP. Then wide receiver: Jalen Coker started and ran for three yards, 0.3, and Germie Bernard started at flex for 1.0, while Omarion Hampton ($47) ran for 105 yards and a touchdown on the bench, 18.0. Josh Jacobs, last week's projected zero, is on injured reserve, which is at least honest. David Njoku was added Monday afternoon and scored 0.00 on the bench. 127.18, 2-0, cleared the median by 2.61. Jon scored 100.86, the lowest score in the league, 0-13 in all-play, with a perfect lineup for the third week running. Perfect again for the same reason: all five bench players scored zero. Colston Loveland, Courtland Sutton, Bo Nix, David Montgomery, Dontayvion Wicks. Adonai Mitchell, the $20 zero, scored 7.4. The one week he shows up, the team does not. A.J. Brown 3.7: 18.3 points in ten weeks for $45, $2.46 a point, the worst money in the league. 4-16, 1-9 against the median.

The house reopened. Patrick Mahomes, a $3 auction quarterback, threw five touchdowns for 348 yards: 35.42. Deebo Samuel ran one in and caught one, 26.04. Derrick Henry, who threw for minus three yards last week, scored twice: 16.5. Drake London 14.9. Devin Lloyd 11.0 at IDP. Evan McPherson, added Wednesday, kicked for 7.4. 155.24, 2-0, three straight 0-2 weeks finished. The bench still had a running back problem: Kaelon Black ($12 last week) 13.6 on the bench for the second straight week, Aaron Jones 12.0, while Breece Hall started for 13.3. Konata Mumpfield, a $5 claim, 10.6 on the bench. Chris Olave ($32) 4.5 in the lineup. 14.60 of regret, which this week counted as restraint. Abhishek lost by 33.58. Trevor Lawrence threw for 352 yards, 27.78, and Isaiah Likely ($3) caught nine balls for 24.2. Then Sunday morning: at 8:53 Khalil Herbert, at 9:00 Barion Brown, both straight into the lineup. Herbert returned kicks for 168 yards, 10.42. Brown returned them for 28, 1.12 at flex. Tank Dell 3.6 at the other flex. 121.66 against a 101.19 projection, the lowest projection in the league, beaten by twenty points, and still 0-2. At 5:24 on Tuesday morning he cut Savion Williams.

Three straight wins for the team the model ranked fourteenth in August. Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught eight balls for 171 yards, 29.1. Parker Washington 27.1, James Cook 23.7, C.J. Stroud ($1) 21.44, Stefon Diggs 17.3. Chris Boswell, a $3 claim, 6.5. 164.48, 12-1 in all-play, 2-0. The bench: Alvin Kamara ($1) scored two touchdowns, 14.9, while Bam Knight started at running back for 2.4. Pat Freiermuth, added Wednesday, 10.5 on the bench while Travis Kelce started for 4.0. Keenan Allen benched again, 8.6. 19.00 points of regret, won by 40.86 anyway. Nathan finally solved the Kirk Cousins file, entry three: Cousins benched for 16.38, Jayden Daniels started for 22.76. Right for the first time. Lost by 40.86. The Colts, a $0 claim, scored a touchdown, 17.76. Tutu Atwell, Nathan's last $7, 3.6 at flex. Tyler Warren 1.4 at tight end on an 11.40 projection. Wan'Dale Robinson 2.5. Malachi Fields 7.7 on the bench. 123.62, missed the median by 0.95, 0-2, and $0 of FAAB left. Down two to seventh. The best luck in the league is starting to run out.

174.40. The highest score of the week and the second-highest of the season, 13-0 in all-play, and the biggest win of the week, 63.84. Christian McCaffrey caught 161 yards and two touchdowns and ran for 62 more: 46.3, the best start of Week 10. Joe Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns, 34.16. Ja'Marr Chase caught eleven for 231 yards, 31.6. Then the bench, because it is Will. Last week Josh Downs started for 3.9 and DeMario Douglas ($40) scored 13.7 on the bench. This week Douglas started for 0.9 and Downs scored 13.7 on the bench. The exact number, the other way round. Matthew Stafford ($1) threw three touchdowns on the bench, 20.76. Seth McGowan 17.64 on the bench. Jason Myers kicked for 3.0. The best lineup scores 194.64, 15.36 more than the season high, sitting on a bench. 89.6 percent, 20.24 of regret. Up three to fifth, still the worst luck in the league. Andrew: sixteen adds, two of them Broncos on a bye, Geno Smith at quarterback for 148 yards and 5.92, Chris Rodriguez Jr. 0.5 at running back. The Vikings, a $5 claim, scored 22.4, the best defense of the week, and Myles Price, added Saturday, 16.9. Puka Nacua on injured reserve, Caleb Williams, D'Andre Swift and Luther Burden on bye. Kaleb Johnson cost $4 on Wednesday and was gone before Sunday. A perfect lineup, 110.56, 1-12 in all-play, 0-2. Down three.
